pr_title: Check testing framework in action text installer
pr_body:
### Summary

Fixes #35053

The goal of this PR is to check if the "spec" directory has been registered in an application and then properly adapt the action_text installer to use the adequate folder so that fixtures don't end up under "test".

I tested this in a local application and it worked, but please let me know if this is the expected implementation.
pr_comments:
~~Since this file is needed at the time of the test run. So in my opinion, it is better to generate it together when the generator generates the test file.~~

~~This will also allow the library(e.g. `rspec-rails`) to add fixtures at the right time. What do you think?~~

(EDITED)

Sorry, I confused Action Text and Action Mailbox. Please ignore this comment.
@y-yagi No problem at all. Do you believe the implementation looks good?

I really thing this is being done at the wrong level. This installer should be a generator, and being a generator we could have different hooks to different test frameworks like others generators have.

@rafaelfranca thanks for the guidance, it helped to get me started.

I've created basic generators using the hooks you mentioned. I have a few doubts before I can continue developing these.

1. With this implementation, the generator runs by running `rails g actiontext`. Is this the desired or should it be `rails g actiontext:install`?
2. Should the javascript portion of the original installer (installing via yarn and appending to the package file) be inside this generator as well? What is the standard way of running a bin file from within a generator?
3. For copying yarn.tt, is there any way I can reuse the app generator? At the moment, I'm simply copying the template, but the app generator runs chmod and other bin related operations that I could reuse.
When fully implemented, I believe this PR will fix #35053, #35003 and #35305. The PR #35088 can be closed since the functionality will be covered by the generator.

It is my personal opinion. 

1. The command the user should execute should remain `action_text:install`. Therefore, I do not think that it is necessary for the name of the generator to be `action_text:install` (I think that it is more important that the process is properly divided for each process). 
2. I think it better to do this. Since the generator is based on thor, you can use the method of thor (in this case surely `run`). 
3. I'm not sure, why need to copy `yarn.tt`? In my feeling that is not should do in the install task.

@y-yagi @rafaelfranca here's the current state of the PR: running `rake action_text:install` will add javascript dependencies, create migrations and templates. I used a local application to try it out and it worked.

Open questions:
1. Should the yarn template be copied in the current way, not be copied or be copied using the app generator?

Please let me know your thoughts and concerns.
My answer remains the same, which is not necessary for this task. I think it is not a process that should be done in this task.
@y-yagi I have pushed a commit to stop copying the yarn template in this generator. Let me know if there are other concerns.
@rafaelfranca do you have any other concerns or requests? I'm available for further improvements so that we can have this merged.

@kaspth @rafaelfranca: refactored the install generator to fit the commented requirements.

Please let me know if there are other improvements you'd like me to work on.

@vinistock thanks for your patience and conquering the many reviews. Railties is one of the most complex and intricate bits to work on when contributing, so an extra big thank you for helping out here 🙏
@kaspth I'm really happy to have helped! I'll keep an eye out for any feedback in case we need to polish it more. Thanks for all the collaboration!

issue_context.title: action_text:install task copies default fixture to /test regardless of testing framework
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
- Have a Rails 6.0.0.beta1 application with a third-party testing framework (`rspec` in this case)
- Run `rails action_text:install`

### Expected behavior
The task can identify the testing framework used (f.x. `rspec`), and copy the default fixture to the right location (`/spec/fixtures`).
Perhaps adding an optional argument to the task to select a testing framework/location manually could help.

### Actual behavior
The task copies the default fixture to `/test/fixtures`, regardless of the testing framework used.

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
6.0.0.beta1

**Ruby version**:
2.6.0

review_comments: Did you try something with `source_root` or similar instead of the constant? That would be more generator like.

I looked at many generators and tried inspecting different methods such as `source_root`, `default_source_root`, `base_root` but didn't find any of them that would point to the root of actiontext. They all either point to `__dir__` or to the railties directory.
When this is called running on master, it attempts to overwrite bin/rails and bin/rake with non-spring versions. Why do we need to call this at all? And if we do, how can we make it aware of spring?

I think it was added to add `bin/yarn`: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/35085/commits/028d1611cdbc36b2650f80661cad6c79bb104051

Since Rails 6 already ships with all the necessary bin, I think we can skip it. I tested by creating new application from the master without updating binstub. Works fine. 

Also, on the master, ActionText installer won't work and silently fail because `@rails/actiontext@^6.1.0-alpha` isn't released yet and installer tries to install the latest version.(PR for same: #37824)

The addition of this evolved from an issue reported that the install of actiontext would fail silently without yarn installed. In my opinion, I do think it's a good idea to make sure the binstubs exist.

However, I'm not sure why the spring bits are not added. Could it be that `app:update:bin` is not matching what `rails new` generates for binstubs? And if so, is that a conscious decision or can we just update it?

@vinistock : I gave it a try by uninstalling yarn from my system on the master branch. Running `rails new` **without yarn** fails with following message. Running `bundle exec rails action_text:install` **without yarn** also fails. The error is not user friendly but yet it doesn't silently fail. I think we should go ahead and remove it and when such case or issue is reported we can rework on it to make it better. Here is the PR to remove it(I am holding that PR since morning, please do close it if not needed): https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/39233

I looked into this a bit further. The root of the issue is that we really only need to make sure `bin/yarn` exists, but we're running the `update:bin` generator which tries to override the binstubs generated by spring.

In my opinion, the ideal would be to surface a way of generating the yarn binstub exclusively (e.g.: `app:update:bin:yarn`). That way we wouldn't mess up the binstubs created by spring and yet be able to provide a nice friendly message about yarn not being installed.

That said, I have no objections to removing it until we figure it out appropriately.

My understanding is that it would involve adding a new task to `railties/lib/rails/tasks/framework.rake` and a dedicated method for only creating `bin/yarn`.
Let's have something that just ensures the yarn bin is available. Rather than overwriting all the other binstubs.
Sounds good. I'll put together a PR and we can iterate on it.
Should/can we assume that `action_text:install:migrations` has set up its dependencies properly and only run it?
Which dependencies are you concerned about? I'd say if there are dependencies, it should check and warn the user if something is missing.

Sorry, I meant task dependencies. If `action_text:install:migrations` require `railties:install:migrations` and `active_storage:install:migrations` first, then shouldn't the Action Text task have those tasks as dependencies?
I have addressed two of your comments. However, I apologize, but it's still not clear to me what code changes implicate from having tasks as dependencies. I didn't find examples.

Let me rephrase just for the record. I would expect the Rake set up to be `task "action_text:install:migrations": [ "active_storage:install:migrations", "railties:install:migrations" ]`. In Rake's parlance when I run the Action Text migration task first run the Active Storage and Railties' migration tasks.

Anyway, I checked up on it and that's not how the tasks are defined. So this is fine.
